properties.name: Tanforan Racetrack
properties.note: racetrack grounds between El Camino Real and the railroad (stables, paddock, parking); 143-acre property sold Mar 1964; Tanforan Park shopping center opened 1971

properties.name: Ford San Jose Assembly Plant
properties.note: plant yard: employee parking, car storage lots and rail sidings between Main St and the Western Pacific line (1961-1980 sheets); plant closed 1983, converted to the Great Mall (opened 22 Sep 1994) - the main assembly building survives inside the mall (today's footprint, which should be dated 1955)

properties.name: Marine World / Africa USA (Redwood Shores)
properties.note: built-up park area (show stadiums, pools, animal areas, lawns) = the magenta built-up tint labelled MARINE WORLD on the 1980 photorevision (1978 photos); opened July 1968, moved to Vallejo 1986; Oracle HQ from 1989

properties.name: Marine World / Africa USA (Redwood Shores)
properties.note: parking lot = dashed outline on the 1980 photorevision

properties.name: Frontier Village
properties.note: amusement-park grounds (green park tint labelled AMUSEMENT PARK, 1973 photorevision): Main Street, rides, narrow-gauge railroad round the perimeter; part became Edenvale Garden Park, the west part housing (Bren)

properties.name: Frontier Village
properties.note: Rainbow Falls trout pond and the canoe canal round Indian Island (Fort Far West): the unshaded area with blue shore lines inside the park tint of the 1973 photorevision (outline includes narrow banks)

properties.name: Frontier Village drive-in (Frontier Auto Movie)
properties.note: drive-in ramps ('Drive-in Theater' label and dashed outline on the 1973 photorevision; outline approximate); opened Apr 1962 (San Jose News ad cited by Cinema Treasures), closed with the park c. 1980 (ESTIMATE)

properties.name: Naval Supply Center Oakland (Naval Supply Depot / FISC Oakland)
properties.note: Naval Supply Center grounds (warehouse blocks, rail sidings, piers) inside its perimeter road on the 1993 sheet; closed 30 Sep 1998 (BRAC 1995), transferred to the Port of Oakland 1999, buildings demolished for the Vision 2000 terminals (Hanjin 2001, SSA 2002) and Middle Harbor Shoreline Park (2004) - end year estimated

properties.name: Emeryville race track (Oakland Trotting Park / New California Jockey Club)
properties.note: one-mile track (2,000 x 900 ft) fitted to the oval of the USGS 1:62,500 San Francisco sheet (1899 edition, 1914 imprint), the sheet shifted 220 m to today's streets, then moved 22 m SW onto the 1911 Sanborn sheets 321/324; track width 18 m estimated; rebuilt Oct 1896 for the New California Jockey Club, racing ended 1911, subdivided into factory sites 1915

properties.name: Emeryville race track (Oakland Trotting Park / New California Jockey Club)
properties.note: infield (Temescal Creek ran through the track)

properties.name: Idora Park: Auto Race Course (electric cars)
properties.note: Auto Race Course (electric cars): track between the two curves of the 1911 sheet, hand-traced; 1911 Sanborn sheet 293 fitted to today's block (affine, residuals 1.5 m); park opened 16 May 1903, closed Jan 1929, razed 1929

properties.name: Idora Park: Amphitheatre (open-air seating and platform)
properties.note: Amphitheatre (open-air seating and platform): dashed outline on the 1911 sheet (uncoloured = open air), hand-traced; 1911 Sanborn sheet 293 fitted to today's block (affine, residuals 1.5 m); park opened 16 May 1903, closed Jan 1929, razed 1929

properties.name: Idora Park: Idora Park grounds
properties.note: Idora Park grounds: the park block (56th-58th St, Telegraph-Shattuck), corners from today's parcels; 16.8 acres (documented 17.5); 1911 Sanborn sheet 293 fitted to today's block (affine, residuals 1.5 m); park opened 16 May 1903, closed Jan 1929, razed 1929

properties.name: Green Arbor Baths open swimming tank
properties.note: Green Arbor Baths open swimming tank: hand-traced on the 1897 Sanborn map (sheet 11); opened c.1878 by John T. Gilman, vanished by 1900 (Alameda Post); outlines from the 1897 Sanborn

properties.name: The Terrace Baths enclosed swimming tank (bay water inside a planked platform)
properties.note: The Terrace Baths enclosed swimming tank (bay water inside a planked platform): hand-traced on the 1897 Sanborn map (sheet 15); opened 1878 by Robert Haley on the SE corner of Central and Third Ave (Sixth St); managed by L. W. Shroeder in 1897-98 (Alameda Post); outlines from the 1897 Sanborn; end ESTIMATED at the building of New Surf Beach / Neptune Beach next door (1916; the 1948 Sanborn shows Neptune Court on the site)

properties.name: Sunny Cove Baths concrete swimming tank
properties.note: Sunny Cove Baths concrete swimming tank: hand-traced on the 1948 Sanborn map (sheet 11); opened 1878 by G. W. Trover beside the Fifth Street station, operated until 1950 (site of the Marina View apartments) (Alameda Post); 1897 buildings until the rebuilding seen on the 1948 Sanborn (midpoint 1922, ESTIMATE)

properties.name: Cottage Baths swimming tank
properties.note: Cottage Baths swimming tank: hand-traced on the 1948 Sanborn map (sheet 12); opened 1895 by William S. Schmidt (Alameda Post); 1897 Sanborn (tub baths) and 1948 Sanborn (swimming tank); gone on the USGS Oakland West 1959 sheet (1958 photos) -> end = midpoint 1953 (ESTIMATE)

properties.name: Neptune Gardens (Long Branch Baths site)
properties.note: Neptune Gardens / Long Branch grounds (lawns, summer houses, pavilion) between the Terrace Baths and Webster St, Central Ave to the 1897 shoreline (Sanborn 1897 sheet 15; outline approximate)

properties.name: Neptune Beach
properties.note: Neptune Beach grounds: Central Ave to the shoreline / breakwater of the USGS Oakland West 1949 sheet (1946 photos: the fill the resort built, taken over by the U.S. Maritime Service training station in 1942), from the shore west of McKay Ave to the fence line east of Webster St; '125 acres' when sold in 1939 (incl. tidelands); outline ESTIMATE

properties.name: Neptune Beach
properties.note: Neptune Beach stadium track (8,000-seat stadium with a track, Alameda Post): oval west of McKay Ave, long axis N-S, PLACED from the 1930s aerial photograph (size and position ESTIMATE)

properties.name: Neptune Beach
properties.note: stadium infield (ESTIMATE)

properties.name: Neptune Beach
properties.note: large swimming pool on fill with fountain and diving platforms (the second, 'Olympic-size' pool), east of the coaster, long axis parallel to Central Ave: PLACED from the 1930s aerial photograph, ~100 x 40 m (ESTIMATE)

properties.name: Neptune Beach
properties.note: first (smaller) swimming pool at the east end of the large pool, PLACED from the 1930s aerial photograph (ESTIMATE)

properties.name: Neptune Beach
properties.note: lawns and picnic grounds (barbecue pits) with walks between the pools and the seawall / promenade, from the 1930s aerial photograph (ESTIMATE)

properties.name: Shell Mound Park: shell mound (bottom line of the mound)
properties.note: shell mound (bottom line of the mound): 1911 Sanborn sheets 323-325 (sheet 325 fitted to today's Park Ave crossings, residuals <= 2.1 m; 324 joined to 325 by the covered walk drawn on both, 323 to 324 by two hydrants: +-5 m on 324, +-15 m on 323); outline approximate (fence lines of the sheets)

properties.name: Shell Mound Park: Shell Mound Park grounds
properties.note: Shell Mound Park grounds: 1911 Sanborn sheets 323-325 (sheet 325 fitted to today's Park Ave crossings, residuals <= 2.1 m; 324 joined to 325 by the covered walk drawn on both, 323 to 324 by two hydrants: +-5 m on 324, +-15 m on 323); outline approximate (fence lines of the sheets)

properties.name: Oaks Park grounds (Oakland Base Ball Association)
properties.note: Oaks Park grounds (Oakland Base Ball Association): playing field; Sanborn Oakland 1911-Oct 1950 vol. 3 sheet 317, 'Oakland Base Ball Association grounds, from plans Feb. 1913', fitted to four street crossings (affine, residual 1.3 m); home of the Oakland Oaks (PCL) 1913-1955; demolished c.1957 (year ESTIMATE); site now Pixar
